bipartite.kami_theme: The speaker declares that she does not grieve over her own fate of being forgotten and abandoned by her lover, despite the vow he once swore.
bipartite.shimo_theme: Instead, her concern shifts entirely to him: she fears for the life of the man who swore that vow, since breaking a sacred oath was believed to invite divine punishment and death.
bipartite.pivot_note: The poem turns on an ironic reversal: one would expect the abandoned woman to lament her own suffering, but the pivot at 'mi o ba omowazu' (I do not think of myself) redirects all emotional weight onto the faithless man's peril — her selfless anxiety for his life becomes a far more piercing reproach than any self-pity could be. The shimo does not resolve the kami's declaration but subverts the listener's expectation of where sympathy should lie.

kigo.note: This poem contains no seasonal imagery; it is a purely emotional/relational poem (koi-uta) concerned with abandonment and broken vows, with no reference to natural phenomena, flora, fauna, or seasonal markers of any kind.

source_jp:
忘らるる
身をば思はず
誓ひてし
人の命の
惜しくもあるかな
